messages.text: Who would you chose mid over balanced ?

I chose **mild because I gave momentum preservation more weight**. Balanced is clearly better for coverage:

| Geometric-primary result | Mild | Balanced |
|---|---:|---:|
| Overall ten-hit coverage | 96.5–96.8% | **98.2%** |
| Worst forward coverage bins | 81–85% | **89–90%** |
| 1 GeV momentum core width change | +1.5%, compatible with no change | **+5.6%, statistically resolved** |
| 1 GeV d0 at \(3.5<|\eta|<4\) | No resolved regression | **11% worse** |

Balanced also gives stronger global impact-parameter gains at 100 GeV.

So **neither layout dominates**. Mild is the more conservative choice under “keep momentum resolution”; balanced is the stronger choice under “approach ten hits everywhere.” The Gaussian cross-check shows a 1 GeV momentum penalty for both, larger for balanced.

If you accept roughly **6% worse low-pT momentum resolution** in exchange for substantially better forward coverage, **I would favour balanced**. My earlier recommendation should have made that weighting more explicit.
